newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry orders in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: German industry orders in line with expectations.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to a report from the economics ministry that German June industry orders climbed 1.5 percent from the month before and were up five percent from a year ago.

GERNOT NERB, SALOMON BROTHERS IN FRANKFURT: "The figure was exactly in line with our expectations. It shows that domestic demand is starting to pick up. The June orders data may now be revised up. The figures help show that the recovery is gaining momentum, its on track. But there is no sign of a capacity utilisation problem. The Bundesbank is now in a more comfortable position. If the dollar doesn't jump above the 1.90 level, they are likely to keep policy on hold and hope that the economic rebound will help the mark."

"Orders were in line with expectations. For the second quarter as a whole, it shows a strong increase from the first quarter. The economy looks on track for 2.4 percent growth for the year as a whole. The question is if this will justify an exchange rate-induced rate hike. But there are no signs that the strong dollar is feeding through into the domestic economy. The Bundesbank would have a hard time selling a rate hike."
